question.problem:
Find the intersection point of the line $l$ and the plane $Π$ with equations

$$
l:r=⟨-1,2,1⟩+t⟨3,0,2⟩,\,Π:r\cdot ⟨1,-1,2⟩=13.
$$
question.worked_solution:
Let's write the equation of the line as

$$
r=⟨-1+3t,2,1+2t⟩.
$$

Now, substituting $r=⟨-1+3t,2,1+2t⟩$ into the equation of the plane, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}r\cdot ⟨1,-1,2⟩ & =13 \\ ⟨-1+3t,2,1+2t⟩\cdot ⟨1,-1,2⟩ & =13 \\ 1(-1+3t)-2+2(1+2t) & =13 \\ -1+3t-2+2+4t & =13 \\ 7t & =14 \\ t & =2.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, position vector $p$ of the intersection point $P$ is obtained by substituting $t=2$ into the equation of the line, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}p & =⟨-1+3(2),2,1+2(2)⟩ \\  & =⟨5,2,5⟩\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the intersection point is $P(5,2,5).$
